name: sidebar
description: A persistent index beside the content. 11 uses across the app and website. The part that is always got wrong is not the look — it is that a sidebar which becomes a drawer on a narrow viewport is still ONE navigation landmark, and duplicating it as a second hidden copy makes a screen reader announce two.

drawer.$description: The same element, moved — not a second copy. `translate` rather than `display:none` so the open state can animate and the DOM keeps one landmark.

reducedMotion.$description: It still opens; it just arrives. Never remove the transform itself — the drawer would then be permanently off-screen.

a11y.note: One `<nav>` with one `aria-label`, in both layouts. As a drawer it needs a focus trap while open, Escape to close, and focus returned to the control that opened it. The current item carries `aria-current=page`; it is not marked by colour alone.
